account:
It is Day 1, eight in the morning, and I am at town hall for my office appointment. I read today's appointment documents this morning and returned them to the appointments chest. The secretary says no new correspondence or business has arrived. I have not personally noticed any unusual activity or evidence of trouble today.

The addition to my usual schedule is a meeting with the innkeeper about the inn's service to town. We agreed yesterday that the innkeeper will meet me at my office today at 17:45, and we will go together to the great hall for 18:00. The secretary recorded this in an approved supplement, and I heard the innkeeper confirm the arrangement this morning. As far as I know, this is ordinary town business; I have no evidence of another purpose.

My other appointments are the mill's grain inspection at 10:00, lunch at home at noon, council letters at the office at 13:00, tea with my neighbour at the dockside cottage on the east bank at 15:00, and a return to the office at 16:30 before the evening meeting. The secretary reports that the neighbour confirmed today's tea. Yesterday the neighbour passed on the baker's news about fresh bread at the market and reported no personally observed trouble or confirmed changes by the river. That is yesterday's report, not a fresh inspection of conditions today.
